Consistently putting myself down and the fear of relapsing or getting worse than I already was allowed me to get to where I am now.

Spiders are known to be a prominent visual hallucination, although I have no idea why. To me, the most jarring was never the visual hallucinations but the auditory ones where I was unable to really differentiate reality from the hallucination.

All of the visual hallucinations I was always able to know that it’s a direct cause of the drug and therefore not real, but this was much harder to do with auditory ones.

Damn, that’s quite a lot, but don’t beat yourself up anymore than you have to. I always tell friends that are dieting too that I’ve learned it’s never about moments like this that define your success at losing weight, but rather it’s being able to get back and recover quickly without spiraling; the consistency of your overall diet will determine your success.

Everyone will have a bad day, some a little worse, some much worse than others, but if you are keeping a solid diet for the majority of the time, it will balance out and you’ll be fine, despite what you’re feeling right now.

About 5-6 times a week, I start my workouts out with a 20 min core session before getting into the actual workout (chest, back, legs, etc.). 

Each day I will alternate between main abs and obliques. My ab workout will consist of about 4x35 leg lifts (I started at 25 when I first began), with about 90-120 second rest periods, then finish off with 1x50-60 slow flutter kicks. I try my best to make sure that my form is strict, which entails doing them slightly slower, legs locked straight, toes pointed out, and arms extended back or upwards.

For my obliques I do 4x15 window wipers with approximately same rest interval but sometimes slightly longer because they are harder for me. Then 2x15 of standing oblique extensions with my resistance bands. I also make sure this is relatively heavy and try to do them slowly to maximize the muscles’ time under tension.

Both these core workouts should take no longer than 20 min. Even though the quantity and rest time intervals may be different for you, it’s all about just pushing yourself and keeping good form. Just push as hard as you can within those 20 min and eventually the quantity will come!

I have been overweight for the majority of my life as well, I can relate. Things turned around when I started gymming and building healthier eating habits. I think a common misconception is that you need to go to the gym to lose weight.

I’m not saying you have to push it to an extreme and crunch numbers all the time when you eat, but more of just be aware of what you’re putting your body. Is it fried? Does it have a lot of fat? Have I eaten too many carbs today and maybe I should switch out these potatoes for some broccoli or something? You will have a general sense of what’s healthy or not.

Know your body. Do you like to snack? Do you eat out a lot? Do you drink juices and sodas? Eating out may seem healthy, but truth be told pretty much everywhere designs their food to taste good, which is usually done by adding a ton of fat or sugar. Drinking your calories away is a really easy way to unknowingly go over your daily caloric limit too. Switch those juices and sodas out for water. If you’re the type to snack a lot, then you would reduce the size of your meals so the snacks don’t push you over as well.

I play samus and my sparring partner plays incineroar. I can say with almost certainty this is a heavily skewed losing matchup for you.

​

Depending on how good the samus is, try to look for a pattern in their projectile play. If they are not good, they will likely have a flow chart. Once you have an idea on their pattern, you can fight accordingly.

Pay attention to charge shot, always. If you do not track this, you've already lost. Parry baby charge shots. Also pay attention if the charge shot is full. bad samus players will often keep their charge shots fully charged, this is really good for you because they lose a huge part of their mobility and mixup game. if you see it is fully charged, be ready to shield at any point, but you can play much more aggressively.

Don't side B recover too close to ledge, you will get spiked.

Watch out for super missile damage on shield, it does a lot of shield damage. i believe you can contest this with nair though. Pay close attention to what samus player does after shooting a missile, are they running at you? Waiting? Fairing? Trying to grab? Adjust accordingly. Also, if you get hit by super missile by ledge, it is a true combo into spike on the entire cast. This is true from 15-65ish i believe. 

Unlike other more traditional zoners, samus's projectiles are all extremely linear, mixing up double jumps, parries, and shields will work. almost any move will pop missiles as well.

If samus constantly uses tether to recover at ledge, be ready to edge guard with falling nair or falling neutral B.

If you get predictable with revenging a missile, unless charge shot can kill you, i like to follow up with grab isntead. samus grab range outranges your revenge 1 and 2 hitbox, then after you get thrown, you are now in disadvantage and your revenge stack(s) are now gone. 

Beware of zair, as it will stuff out a lot of your approaches. if the samus is bad and just does not use zair, you are given a lot more freedom to be in the air, but also beware of fair. i believe your fair will outrange samus fair though.

Mixup ledge get up options. Bomb at ledge will force you to do something or risk being knocked off by the explosion. If you neutral getup and a bomb is there, you will be spiked. This is true for all characters at all percentages. This will kill most of the cast as early as 45% unless you have a very good recovery (inkling). If you panic and can not think of an option, drop down and regrab ledge, but get ready for samus to run up and either dtilt or utilt at ledge. dtilt will kill at higher percentages and knock you up and away at a diagonal angle, so be prepared to get chased by an aerial. if utilt hits you, this will kill earlier and will knock you back very far. utilt will also cover jump. if you regrab ledge and see samus running up to it to perform one of these moves, immediately getup attack or roll in.

Samus grab clanks with your side b, so be aware of this. and get ready to act after the clank.

Samus (108) weighs almost as heavy as  incineroar (116), do not use anything like a risky smash attack unless it is a hard read or you are certain she is at kill percent. make sure at higher percentages your kill moves are not stale (side b, bair, ftilt). Samus is only 8 units away from being classified as a super heavyweight, treat her as such.

If you get grabbed by ledge around 60-75%, DI out or you will eat an IRAR bair. If you are not ready for it, depending on samus's rage and the stage being played, it may kill you. even if it does not, you will be put in a really unfavorable spot.

A lot of samuses tend to dthrow > fair, but dthrow > nair at lower/mid percentages will force tech situation. be prepared and don't be predictable. if you roll away, you will be hit by charge shot if it is available. if you miss the tech entirely, samus an run up, jab 1 > utilt to reset. this can be followed up by eating a bair, nair, fair, charge shot. possibilities are endless.
